body_text: View All News VENU Hosts Special Event for Ford Amphitheater Investors Featuring VENU Shareholder Dierks Bentley July 7, 2026 COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Venu Holding Corporation ("VENU" or the "Company") (NYSE AMERICAN: VENU), an owner, operator, and developer of premium live entertainment destinations, today announced it hosted a dedicated evening for Colorado based Ford Amphitheater Luxe FireSuite® and Owners Club investors, featuring GRAMMY-nominated, multi-platinum recording artist and VENU® shareholder Dierks Bentley. Dierks Bentley Unplugged Pre-Party in Colorado Springs, CO | Photo Credit: Keni Mac The event took place Thursday, July 2nd, at Phil Long Music Hall at Bourbon Brothers, ahead of Bentley's performance on the Company's Ford Amphitheater main stage as part of his Off the Map tour, marking his return to Ford Amphitheater this summer. The evening included a curated question and answer session with VENU Chief Operating Officer, Vic Sutter, and a live acoustic performance of several of Bentley's most beloved hits, giving shareholders a rare, close-up look at the artist whose stake in VENU, and role as a founding member of the Company's celebrity advisory council, have helped shape VENU's approach to venue design and fan experience. The advisory council curates VENU's development, the growth of its premium entertainment campuses, and the elevation of its hospitality experiences, bringing together industry leaders who have built and shaped the live entertainment landscape. "Experiences like this are one in a million," said J.W. Roth, Founder, Chairman, and CEO of VENU. "Dierks represents everything we're building toward: authenticity, excellence, and an unwavering commitment to the fan experience. I'm grateful he could spend this time with fellow shareholders and for the opportunity to host him and his entire team.” VENU continues to grow its national footprint, with venues operating and in development or entitlement across Colorado, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas, and additional markets in pre-construction phases. The Company's approach of aligning artists, fans, and shareholders around its venues remains central to its long-term growth strategy. For additional details, visit venu.live. About Venu Holding Corporation Venu Holding Corporation ("VENU") (NYSE American: VENU) is a premier owner, developer, and operator of luxury, experience-driven entertainment destinations. Founded by Colorado Springs entrepreneur J.W. Roth, VENU has a portfolio of premium brands that includes Ford Amphitheater, Sunset Amphitheaters, Phil Long Music Hall, The Hall at Bourbon Brothers, Bourbon Brothers Smokehouse and Tavern, Aikman Owners Clubs, and Roth’s Sea & Steak. With venues operating and in development across Colorado, Georgia, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas and a nationwide expansion underway, VENU is setting a new standard for live entertainment. VENU has been recognized nationally by The Wall Street Journal , The New York Times , Billboard , VenuesNow , and Variety for its innovative and disruptive approach to live entertainment. Through strategic partnerships with industry leaders such as AEG Presents, NFL Hall of Famer and Founder of EIGHT Elite Light Beer, Troy Aikman, Billboard, Aramark Sports + Entertainment, Tixr, Boston Common Golf, Niall Horan, and Dierks Bentley, VENU continues to shape the future of the entertainment landscape. title: AI Moneyball: How PlayVision is Revolutionizing College Basketball's Transfer Portal
body_text: The Old Game: Tradition, Talent Gaps, and a Manual Lens into the Transfer Portal's Wild West The college basketball transfer portal is only six years old, but it has already transformed recruitment dynamics across the sport. With collegiate athletes now able to be paid, the game is undergoing shifts in processes and strategies—much like many other industries. Historically, college basketball has operated within a hierarchy dominated by blue blood programs, creating a wide talent gap among the 350 Division-1 men's teams. Only 15 programs have won multiple championships. At first glance, the transfer portal seems to widen that gap. Bigger market teams attract more NIL money and use it aggressively to win over the best players. It has become like an auction, where players follow the bigger check instead of tradition, culture, or academic fit. For smaller programs in power conferences and mid-majors, limited coaching staffs are overwhelmed trying to manually track thousands of players and stats. At first glance, the future may look bleak—but college basketball has always thrived on the underdog spirit. March Madness is chaos and excitement, where unknown teams can topple household names. It's David versus Goliath — but David doesn't wield Goliath's sword. Instead, he has his own. The New Era: AI-Driven Analysis Leveling the Playing Field for Every Team At PlayVision AI, we're leveraging AI and ML to turn this upheaval into opportunity, helping every team compete smarter and stronger. Traditional scouting and recruiting simply can't keep pace with the speed and complexity the transfer portal demands. Coaches and scouts crave tools to spot diamonds in the rough—players who can change the game. That's what Moneyball was about, right? We're here to take it even further. This past season, over 2,300 players entered the transfer portal—roughly 41% of all Division-1 men's basketball players. While the top 50-100 players often have clear landing spots, many teams scramble to rebuild rosters that look completely different week to week. PlayVision identified these trends early and used AI to tackle them head-on. Using a proprietary algorithm, we ranked all 5,607 players based on offensive and defensive skill, efficiency, and usage. This gave birth to our game-changer: the PlayVision Player Index (PPI)—a data-driven edge once reserved for blue blood programs, now accessible to schools of every size. Take Yaxel Lendeborg, a senior from the University of Alabama at Birmingham. While respected within his conference, teams at higher levels underestimated him, doubting a mid-major player could top our leaderboard. But we stood firm. We analyzed his ability to get to the rim, his efficient outside shooting at over 35% despite standing 6'10", his accurate passing, and the advantages created when he attacks the paint—quantifying every detail. Yaxel earned a 91.8 PPI, the highest of any player in the transfer portal and the fourth highest nationally—trailing only Cooper Flagg (95.0), Johni Broome (94.9), and Collin Murray-Boyles (92.0), all projected first-round draft picks. Teams took notice. Yaxel skyrocketed from being unranked as a junior to becoming the consensus top player in the transfer portal, ultimately forgoing the NBA draft to sign with the University of Michigan for $4 million. His decision reflects a growing trend: with rising NIL money, staying in college can now be more lucrative than going pro. But the PPI isn't just for the elite. Schools at every level—Power 5, mid-major, even Ivy League—use these metrics to break down players. The University of Florida won a national championship this year with three of its top five players coming from mid-major schools. Imagine access to hundreds of stats—dribbles, off-ball actions, passing tendencies—that reveal a player's true worth beyond money. This is college basketball: chaotic, thrilling, and now more insightful than ever. AI won't take away the game we love—it will enhance it. With 350 Division-1 men's teams, let's create a world where every team has a chance. PlayVision AI is the key to that future.

title: Clasificación UL 94 y materiales plásticos retardantes de llama
summary: Un análisis detallado de los materiales termoplásticos con características retardantes de llama así como de la clasificación UL 94.
body_text: Si está diseñando con plástico y no ha tenido en cuenta las clasificaciones de inflamabilidad, está arriesgando mucho más que el cumplimiento normativo. UL 94 no es solo una etiqueta. Es un garante. La diferencia entre una clasificación V-0 y V-2 puede suponer la diferencia entre una producción aprobada y un costoso rediseño. Por ejemplo, si alguna vez ha visto cómo una pieza perfectamente diseñada no superaba la certificación porque el espesor de su pared era inferior al umbral de la prueba, sepa que esto ocurre más de lo que piensa. Aplicaciones para plásticos retardantes de llama Los materiales con clasificación UL 94 se utilizan habitualmente en: Componentes del compartimento del motor de automóviles (PA, PPS) Ventiladores de refrigeración y soportes (PBT, LCP) Cajas eléctricas y carcasas para interruptores (PC, mezclas de ABS/PC) Guías para cables industriales y componentes electrónicos (PP, PEEK) Carcasas de productos sanitarios (PPSU) Carcasas para conectores y hardware de telecomunicaciones (ABS, PC/ABS) Estas piezas suelen estar expuestas a temperaturas elevadas, cargas mecánicas y proximidad a corrientes eléctricas, por lo que sus propiedades retardantes de llama son fundamentales para la seguridad y el cumplimiento normativo. ¿Qué es UL 94? Analicemos qué significa realmente UL 94, por qué es más importante de lo que la mayoría de la gente cree y cómo tomar decisiones más inteligentes sobre los materiales desde el principio. UL 94 es una norma sobre inflamabilidad de los plásticos desarrollada por Underwriters Laboratories. Evalúa cómo reaccionan los plásticos ante una llama abierta, midiendo el tiempo de ignición, el comportamiento de autoextinción y si el goteo de material inflamado enciende un indicador secundario de algodón. La norma UL 94 es compatible con otras normas internacionales, lo que le confiere relevancia mundial para los ensayos de seguridad contra incendios. Las configuraciones de ensayo varían. La clasificación HB comprende una evaluación de la combustión horizontal. Otras clasificaciones, como las series V y 5V, utilizan barras o placas verticales. Dentro de la serie V, la diferencia entre V-0 y V-1 es que un material V-0 cumple un nivel más alto de criterios en las mismas condiciones de ensayo. Las condiciones de ensayo son más estrictas al pasar del grupo de clasificación V al 5V, ya que los ensayos de 5V requieren un mayor nivel de resistencia a la inflamabilidad. Clasificaciones UL 94 de un vistazo Clasificación Criterios principales HB Combustión lenta en una pieza horizontal V-2 La llama se extingue en 30 segundos en la pieza; se admite el goteo de plástico inflamable en vertical V-1 La llama se extingue en 30 segundos en una pieza vertical; se admite el goteo de plástico sin llama V-0 La llama se extingue en 10 segundos en una pieza vertical; se admite el goteo de plástico sin llama 5VB La llama se extingue en 60 segundos en una pieza vertical; no se admite el goteo de plástico sin llama. En las muestras de ensayo, se puede producir un agujero 5VA Igual que 5VB, pero no se debe producir un agujero en la placa. Es la clasificación más alta de la norma UL 94. La llama se extingue en 60 segundos en una pieza vertical; no se admite el goteo de plástico sin llama. En las muestras de ensayo, no se puede producir un agujero La clasificación de los materiales como 5VA o 5VB implica un ensayo de combustión vertical de 125 mm utilizando la llama de un mechero Bunsen. Las barras y placas tienen requisitos específicos de tamaño y espesor, y la aplicación de la llama se realiza en intervalos de cinco segundos con cinco segundos sin llama entre cada aplicación. En la serie V, se aplica una llama de 20 mm dos veces durante diez segundos cada vez. La segunda llama se aplica una vez que la muestra ya no tiene llama o inmediatamente si nunca se enciende. Configuraciones de ensayo UL 94 Ensayo de combustión horizontal Ensayo de combustión vertical de 20 mm Ensayo de combustión vertical de 125 mm (barra) Ensayo de combustión vertical de 125 mm (placa) Retardante de llama vs. resistente a la llama: ¿ cuál es la diferencia? Los materiales retardantes de llama están diseñados para ralentizar la ignición y suprimir la propagación de las llamas. Pueden inflamarse, pero se autoextinguen una vez que se elimina la fuente de ignición. Las clasificaciones UL 94 se incluyen en esta categoría. Los materiales resistentes a la llama, por el contrario, resisten completamente la ignición y se utilizan a menudo en textiles o equipos de protección personal. Se someten a ensayo según diferentes normas, como ASTM D6413 o ISO 15025. Comprender esta distinción ayuda a los ingenieros a seleccionar los materiales basándose tanto en el rendimiento funcional como en el cumplimiento normativo. Por qué son importantes el espesor y la formulación Las clasificaciones UL 94 dependen del espesor. Una resina que supera el ensayo con un espesor de 1,5 mm (0,059 in) puede no superarla con un espesor de 0,74 mm (0,029 in). Algunos materiales ofrecen un rendimiento constante en una amplia gama de espesores de pared, pero esto no está garantizado. La formulación también desempeña un papel fundamental. La mayoría de las calidades retardantes de llama dependen de aditivos específicos para cumplir los objetivos de rendimiento. Incluso pequeñas modificaciones (como cambiar los colorantes) pueden invalidar la certificación, a menos que la nueva mezcla se someta a ensayos y se certifique de forma independiente. En caso de duda, solicite a su proveedor de materiales una Tarjeta amarilla UL, una certificación que acredita que el material ha superado ensayos de seguridad y rendimiento. Debe cubrir la formulación completa y el rango de espesor requerido. Materiales retardantes de llama disponibles en Protolabs Ofrecemos una variedad de materiales con clasificación UL 94 para moldeo por inyección e impresión 3D . También pueden evaluarse resinas suministradas por el cliente previa solicitud. Tenga en cuenta que un mismo material puede tener diferentes clasificaciones en función de diversos factores, por lo que no se puede afirmar simplemente que un material tiene la clasificación V-0. Además de las decenas de materiales con clasificación UL 94 disponibles para moldeo por inyección, hemos añadido dos materiales retardantes de llama para impresión 3D: ESD Black (Loctite 3380) Esta resina tiene una clasificación UL 94 V-0 en espesores de 2,0 mm (0,08 in). Añade capacidades de disipación electrostática (ESD) y funciona bien en piezas impresas que requieren alta precisión y detalles finos. Arkema FR512 Este fotopolímero retardante de llama, utilizado en nuestro proceso HPS, obtiene la clasificación UL 94 V-0 en espesores de 0,79 mm (0,031 in). Es ideal para piezas intrincadas que requieren una resolución detallada y propiedades retardantes del fuego certificadas. Más información sobre los materiales retardantes de llama para impresión 3D Los PFAS en los materiales ignífugos Las sustancias perfluoroalquílicas y polifluoroalquílicas (PFAS) se han utilizado durante mucho tiempo en aditivos ignífugos por su excepcional resistencia térmica y química. Sin embargo, los PFAS se enfrentan actualmente a una presión regulatoria cada vez mayor debido a su persistencia en el medio ambiente y a su relación con posibles riesgos para la salud. Aunque algunos materiales ignífugos siguen conteniendo PFAS, muchos fabricantes están dejando de utilizarlos. Seguimos de cerca la normativa sobre PFAS. Aunque actualmente el contenido de PFAS no figura en los datos de nuestros materiales, animamos a los clientes con inquietudes normativas o medioambientales a ponerse en contacto con nosotros. Podemos ayudarle a explorar alternativas o a confirmar composiciones específicas de resinas cuando sea necesario. Consideraciones medioambientales Los retardantes de llama mejoran la seguridad contra incendios, pero pueden complicar la gestión de los productos al final de su vida útil. Los aditivos halogenados son difíciles de separar durante el reciclaje y pueden liberar compuestos tóxicos si se incineran. Por este motivo, existe un interés creciente por los retardantes de llama no halogenados, que ofrecen un rendimiento similar con un menor impacto medioambiental. La selección de materiales debe tener siempre en cuenta tanto la seguridad como la sostenibilidad. Por qué son importantes las clasificaciones de resistencia al fuego en el desarrollo de productos Las clasificaciones UL 94 no son solo detalles técnicos. A menudo determinan si una pieza puede utilizarse en sectores regulados, como el aeroespacial, el médico, el automovilístico y el de la electrónica de consumo. Elegir desde el principio un material certificado con clasificación de resistencia al fuego ayuda a evitar problemas de cumplimiento normativo, costosos rediseños y fallos en la certificación en fases avanzadas del proyecto. Una cosa más antes de enviar su diseño La certificación UL es específica para cada formulación. Una resina puede tener una «tarjeta amarilla», pero las mezclas personalizadas, los colorantes, los aditivos y otras modificaciones del material base pueden afectar a su clasificación. Si trabaja en sectores en los que se aplican múltiples normas de propiedades, como las relativas al humo, la toxicidad o el envejecimiento térmico, asegúrese de validar el perfil completo del material antes de la producción. Para obtener más información sobre las propiedades de los materiales de moldeo por inyección, lea nuestra Guía de selección de materiales para moldeo por inyección . La norma UL 94 puede parecer una letra pequeña de la normativa, pero desempeña un papel determinante en lo que se fabrica, lo que se aprueba y lo que se señala para su rediseño. Nuestros ingenieros de aplicaciones están a su disposición para ayudarle a tomar la decisión adecuada para su aplicación, presupuesto y calendario. Solicita un presupuesto ¿Estás listo para elegir un material con certificación UL 94 y evitar costosos rediseños? Sube tu pieza para obtener al instante el precio y los plazos de entrega. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Qué es la norma UL 94 y por qué es importante? expand_less expand_more La norma UL 94 es una norma de inflamabilidad de plásticos de Underwriters Laboratories que evalúa cómo reaccionan los materiales ante una llama abierta, la ignición y el comportamiento autoextinguible, así como si las gotas incandescentes prenden fuego a un indicador de algodón. Es una norma ampliamente reconocida y a menudo exigida en sectores regulados, por lo que la clasificación que elijas puede determinar si una pieza supera la certificación o debe rediseñarse. ¿Qué significan las principales clasificaciones de la norma UL 94 (HB, V y 5V)? expand_less expand_more HB: Combustión lenta en una muestra horizontal. V-2: La muestra vertical deja de arder en un plazo de 30 segundos; se permiten gotas ardientes que puedan inflamar el algodón. V-1: La muestra vertical deja de arder en un plazo de 30 segundos; no se permiten gotas ardientes que inflamen el algodón. V-0: La muestra vertical deja de arder en un plazo de 10 segundos; no se permiten gotas ardientes que inflamen el algodón. 5VB/5VA: Ensayos verticales más estrictos que utilizan una llama mayor; no se permiten gotas incandescentes. La norma 5VB permite la perforación (agujeros), mientras que la 5VA, la clasificación más alta de UL 94, no lo permite. ¿Cómo influyen el grosor de la pieza y la composición en la clasificación UL 94? expand_less expand_more Las clasificaciones dependen del espesor y son específicas para cada formulación. Una resina que cumpla con la clasificación V-0 a 1,5 mm puede no cumplirla a 0,8 mm, e incluso pequeños cambios en la formulación (como un nuevo colorante) pueden invalidar una clasificación anterior. Confírmelo siempre con la «Tarjeta Amarilla» de UL del material y asegúrese de que cubre exactamente su formulación y rango de espesor. ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre los materiales ignífugos y los resistentes al fuego? expand_less expand_more Los materiales ignífugos están diseñados para retrasar la ignición y autoextinguirse una vez que se elimina la fuente de llama (en este caso se aplica la norma UL 94). Los materiales resistentes al fuego están diseñados para impedir por completo la ignición y se someten a ensayos conforme a otras normas (por ejemplo, ASTM D6413, ISO 15025), que se utilizan habitualmente para textiles y equipos de protección individual (EPI). ¿Qué materiales ignífugos ofrece Protolabs? ¿Y qué hay de los PFAS y las preocupaciones medioambientales? expand_less expand_more Protolabs ofrece numerosas resinas con clasificación UL 94 para moldeo por inyección y opciones ignífugas seleccionadas para la impresión 3D. Ejemplo: Arkema FR512 (fotopolímero) alcanza la clasificación UL 94 V-0 con un espesor de 0,031 pulgadas (0,79 mm). Las resinas suministradas por el cliente pueden evaluarse previa solicitud. Tenga en cuenta que las clasificaciones varían según el tipo y el espesor; no dé por sentado que se trata de un «V-0» general. Algunos sistemas ignífugos pueden incluir PFAS o aditivos halogenados; supervisamos la normativa y podemos ayudarle a confirmar la composición de la resina o a explorar alternativas no halogenadas para apoyar la reciclabilidad y los objetivos medioambientales.

title: Seroquel (Quetiapine) Uses and Side Effects — Talkspace
summary: Learn about Seroquel (quetiapine) uses, dosage, side effects, safety warnings, and interactions to help you take this medication safely and effectively.
body_text: Key Takeaways Seroquel (quetiapine) is an FDA-approved atypical antipsychotic used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and its extended-release form can be added to antidepressants to treat major depressive disorder. Common Seroquel side effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness, and weight gain, while serious risks may involve metabolic changes and movement disorders. A psychiatric provider can evaluate your symptoms, determine whether Seroquel is appropriate for you, and monitor your health throughout treatment. Seroquel (also known under its generic name quetiapine) is among the most commonly prescribed psychiatric medications in the U.S., yet it is often misunderstood. Whether your healthcare provider just recommended it or you're researching a loved one's prescription, knowing what's actually in the FDA labeling can help you feel more prepared. Seroquel (generic name: quetiapine) is an FDA-approved atypical antipsychotic with uses to treat symptoms of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and depression. Understanding both its common side effects and serious risks can help you use Seroquel safely and have informed conversations with your healthcare provider. What is Seroquel and How Does it Work? Seroquel belongs to a class called atypical antipsychotics, the second generation of antipsychotic drugs. Both contain quetiapine as the active ingredient, but it comes in two formulations: immediate-release (IR) extended-release (XR) Each formulation has distinct FDA-approved uses, which your healthcare provider will use to determine which one fits your treatment plan. What type of drug is Seroquel? Seroquel is classified as an atypical (second-generation) antipsychotic. This classification distinguishes it from older antipsychotic medications and reflects differences in how it interacts with brain chemistry. It's indicated for serious mental health conditions, including schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. How does quetiapine affect the brain? The FDA labeling states that the mechanism behind quetiapine's effectiveness is "unclear," but notes it could be mediated through antagonism at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. An active metabolite called norquetiapine has similar D2 activity and greater 5-HT2A activity than the parent compound. This may contribute to the drug's overall effects. What are the available forms and strengths? Both immediate release and extended release formulations come in multiple tablet strengths, outlined below: Formulation Available strengths Seroquel IR (immediate-release) 25 mg, 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg, 300 mg, 400 mg Seroquel XR (extended-release) 50 mg, 150 mg, and additional strengths Your healthcare provider will select the right form and strength based on your diagnosis, health history, and any other medications you're taking. Which Conditions Does Seroquel Treat? Seroquel's FDA-approved uses span several serious mental health conditions, with meaningful differences between the IR and XR formulations. Knowing which version covers what — and in which populations — helps you have more informed conversations at your next appointment. How is Seroquel used for schizophrenia? Seroquel (quetiapine) is an antipsychotic medication approved to treat schizophrenia in adults and adolescents aged 13 and older. It works by changing the activity of certain natural substances in the brain, helping reduce symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. As per StatPearls , the effective dose range is 150 to 750 mg per day in adults. Adolescents start at lower doses, with the medication gradually adjusted based on response and tolerability. It is taken daily and requires long-term use for continued symptom management. How does Seroquel treat bipolar disorder? Seroquel (quetiapine) is used across all three phases of bipolar disorder, making it one of the more versatile medications in its treatment. Here's how it works at each stage: Mania: Helps calm racing thoughts, reduce agitation, and stabilize mood during manic episodes Depression: Works to lift low mood and improve sleep and energy levels during depressive episodes Maintenance: Taken long-term to reduce how often episodes occur and how severe they are, either alone or alongside other mood stabilizers. Is Seroquel used for depression? Seroquel XR is FDA-approved as an add-on to antidepressants for adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) who haven't had an adequate response to antidepressant treatment alone. Here are a few key points about this use: Only the XR formulation — not IR — carries the MDD indication It functions as an adjunct therapy, not a standalone depression treatment FDA approval is based on two 6-week clinical trials Trial doses were 150 mg/day and 300 mg/day; your healthcare provider will determine the right dose for you Exploring depression treatment options with both a therapist and a psychiatric provider gives you a fuller picture of what's available for your specific situation. How Should You Take Seroquel Safely? Getting Seroquel right involves more than swallowing a pill each day. Careful dose titration, clear missed-dose rules, and a solid plan for discontinuation are all part of safe treatment, and they're worth understanding before Day 1. What is the recommended dosing and titration schedule? Doses always start low and increase gradually. FDA labeling for bipolar mania (IR) shows a starting dose of 50 mg twice daily on Day 1, reaching a total of 400 mg/day by Day 4, with further increases possible up to 800 mg/day by Day 6. Your exact schedule depends on your diagnosis, the formulation prescribed, and how your body responds. What should you do if you miss a dose? The Seroquel XR Medication Guide offers three clear steps for a missed dose: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it's close to your next scheduled dose, skip the missed one. Never take two doses at the same time unless your healthcare provider has specifically directed you to. Can you stop Seroquel suddenly? Stopping Seroquel abruptly is not advised. Sudden discontinuation can cause withdrawal effects, including insomnia, nausea, and vomiting. Any reduction or discontinuation should happen only with your healthcare provider's guidance. For teens managing psychiatric medication alongside school and daily life, connecting with online therapy for teens can offer additional support as they work through treatment. "It is important to titrate a medication like Seroquel by starting at a low dose to establish tolerability, and then increasing slowly until a therapeutic dose is reached where a noticeable positive effect is noted in symptoms. This typically also means more frequent follow ups are needed to work on increasing the dose and monitoring for side effects. If a patient is wanting to discontinue a medication like Seroquel, then tapering slowly is recommended. This way there is time for monitoring for symptoms returning and any side effects with lowering the dose can be minimized." - Talkspace Therapist, Svetlana Stuck, PA-C What are the Common and Serious Side Effects Of Seroquel? Knowing the difference between expected Seroquel side effects and signs that need immediate attention can make early treatment far less stressful, and far safer. What are the most common side effects of Seroquel? Like all antipsychotic medications, Seroquel carries a range of side effects, from common and manageable to serious and requiring prompt medical attention. The table below outlines what to watch for. Category Side effect What to know Common side effects Somnolence, dry mouth, dizziness, constipation Reported at higher rates than placebo in bipolar depression trials of Seroquel IR Additional common effects Increased appetite, upset stomach, fatigue Listed in the Seroquel XR Medication Guide Weight Weight gain The Seroquel XR Medication Guide advises monitoring weight throughout treatment Metabolic effects High blood sugar, increased cholesterol, and triglycerides Can occur even in people without diabetes; blood sugar should be checked before starting treatment Tardive dyskinesia Uncontrolled, repetitive movements May develop during treatment and can persist Neuroleptic malignant syndrome Muscle stiffness, fever, and confusion Rare but serious; requires urgent medical care Suicidal risk Increased risk of suicidal thoughts or actions Particularly in children, teens, and young adults, during the first months of treatment If you or someone you know is experiencing thoughts of suicide, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. What is the black-box warning for Seroquel? Seroquel XR labeling includes the FDA’s most serious safety designation, a black-box warning, which applies to a specific high-risk population. This warning does not reflect the overall safety profile for the conditions Seroquel is approved to treat. The table below summarizes the key points from the Seroquel XR Medication Guide. Warning element Detail Population at risk Elderly people with dementia-related psychosis Identified risk Increased risk of death FDA position Seroquel XR is not approved for treating psychosis in elderly patients with dementia If you're a caregiver for an older adult, this is an essential conversation to have with their healthcare provider before starting any antipsychotic medication. "Once Seroquel is started, a low dose is typically used to allow the body to adjust to the medication, minimize side effects, and allow time to monitor tolerability of the medication. This helps lessen more serious side effects and risks with the medication. Also, when only one medication is started/adjusted at a time, this also allows for more clarity should side effects arise to be able to pinpoint what is contributing to the side effects, whether they are common, and potentially transient ones, or if they are more concerning and require swift action. - Talkspace Therapist, Svetlana Stuck, PA-C Which Drugs and Substances Interact With Seroquel? Quetiapine is processed through a specific enzyme pathway in the body, making it sensitive to other medications that affect that same pathway. Sharing a complete medication list is one of the most protective steps you can take. Which medications should not be taken with Seroquel? FDA labeling identifies CYP3A4 as the enzyme primarily responsible for quetiapine metabolism. Certain drugs that strongly inhibit this enzyme can raise Seroquel levels significantly, increasing the risk of side effects. Your healthcare provider will review your full medication list to identify any combinations that require adjustment or avoidance. What drugs require caution with Seroquel? Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors are the primary concern. The Seroquel XR label identifies examples, including ketoconazole, itraconazole, indinavir, ritonavir, and nefazodone. Both the IR and XR labels indicate that when taken alongside potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, the Seroquel dose may need to be reduced to one-sixth of the original. That's a significant adjustment, which is exactly why complete medication transparency with your healthcare provider matters. Can food or alcohol interact with Seroquel? Alcohol is a documented concern, with a clinical trial referenced in Seroquel IR labeling finding that quetiapine increased the cognitive and motor-impairing effects of alcohol. The label advises limiting alcoholic beverages, and patient labeling warns that alcohol may worsen Seroquel side effects. How Can You Monitor and Manage Risks While On Seroquel? Regular monitoring isn't a sign that something is wrong; it's a standard part of safe psychiatric treatment. Staying on top of recommended checkups helps your psychiatric provider catch early changes before they become bigger problems. This is especially relevant for younger adults; check out mental health tips for college students if you're managing psychiatric care for the first time. What tests and checkups are required? The Seroquel XR Medication Guide advises checking blood sugar before starting treatment and monitoring it during therapy in at-risk patients. It also recommends tracking weight throughout treatment. Given quetiapine's documented effects on blood sugar, cholesterol, and triglycerides, expect your healthcare provider to schedule blood work and physical measurements at regular intervals alongside your medication reviews. How can you reduce side effect risks? No single strategy eliminates risk, but the metabolic concerns in FDA labeling point toward several general areas worth discussing with your healthcare provider: Monitoring blood sugar and cholesterol levels through diet and physical activity Tracking weight consistently throughout treatment Staying hydrated and eating enough fiber to help manage dry mouth and constipation When should you contact a doctor? Some changes require prompt medical attention. Don't wait for your next scheduled appointment if you experience: Signs of high blood sugar, including increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurred vision Uncontrolled or unusual body movements (possible tardive dyskinesia) High fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, or excessive sweating (possible Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome) New or worsening thoughts of suicide or self-harm Extreme drowsiness or dizziness that affects your ability to function safely How Can Online Psychiatry Support Patients Taking Seroquel Safely? Taking medications like Seroquel safely requires ongoing support from a qualified professional who can monitor your response, adjust doses when needed, and watch for side effects over time. Psychiatry plays a central role in that process, going beyond prescribing medication to include regular check-ins, metabolic monitoring, and collaborative decision-making between you and your psychiatric provider. Talkspace psychiatry connects you with licensed psychiatric providers online, making consistent expert care more accessible. Whether you are starting Seroquel or have been on it for a while, an online psychiatrist can assess your symptoms, history, and offer a personalized treatment plan. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Can Seroquel be used as a sleep aid? Seroquel is sometimes prescribed off-label for sleep, but it is primarily an antipsychotic and not approved as a standard sleep aid. Using it solely for sleep carries risks and should only be done under a healthcare provider’s supervision. How long does Seroquel take to work? Seroquel’s effects can vary depending on the condition being treated and the individual. Some people may notice improvements in mood, sleep, or agitation within a few days, while full benefits for conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder may take several weeks. Does Seroquel cause weight gain? Yes, Seroquel can cause weight gain, which is a common side effect. The risk and amount of weight gain vary by individual, dosage, and duration of use. Is it safe to drive while taking Seroquel? Seroquel can cause drowsiness, dizziness, or slowed reaction times, so it may impair your ability to drive or operate machinery safely. It’s best to avoid driving until you know how the medication affects you and to follow your healthcare provider’s guidance. What is the safest way to discontinue Seroquel? The safest way to discontinue Seroquel is to taper the dose gradually under a healthcare provider’s supervision. Abruptly stopping the medication can cause withdrawal symptoms or a return of the underlying condition. Sources U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Drug label: [drug name]. title: Best Tonneau Covers for the Nissan Frontier and Titan: Complete Worksport Buying Guide
summary: Complete Worksport buying guide for Nissan Frontier and Nissan Titan owners comparing AL4, AL3, SC3, SC4, NEXUS, and SOLIS tonneau cover options.
body_text: Best Tonneau Covers for the Nissan Frontier and Titan: Complete Worksport Buying Guide 🌟 Introduction Nissan's truck lineup covers a lot of ground. The Frontier is one of America's best-selling midsize pickups, beloved for its durability, off-road chops, and manageable footprint. The Titan is Nissan's full-size contender — a capable, comfortable workhorse that competes head-to-head with the F-150, Silverado, and Ram 1500. Different trucks, different missions, but they share one need: a quality tonneau cover. This guide walks through every Worksport tonneau cover available for the Nissan Frontier and Titan, helping you figure out which model fits your year, your bed size, and the way you actually use your truck. 🔍 Why This Guide Covers Both the Frontier and the Titan The Frontier and Titan are paired here because they share the same brand, but the selection logic is completely different for each. Frontier owners are typically choosing a tonneau cover for a midsize bed (5'0" or 6'0"), while Titan owners are choosing for a full-size bed (5'6" or 6'6"). These bed sizes determine which Worksport part numbers apply — a Frontier cover will never interchange with a Titan cover, even within the same product line. The two trucks also attract different buyers. Frontier owners tend to prioritize off-road functionality and light payload management. Titan owners often skew toward heavier cargo use and daily work duty. Worksport's lineup — from the lightweight soft SC3 , to the flip-up hard AL4 — offers options for both personalities. 🛻 Nissan Frontier: Two Generations, Two Different Fitments The Nissan Frontier underwent a complete redesign in 2022. The third-generation (2022–present, known internally as the D41) is a from-the-ground-up new platform — new frame, new powertrain, new bed dimensions. The outgoing second-generation (2005–2021, D40 platform) was sold largely unchanged for 17 years, making it one of the longest-running truck designs in automotive history. This matters for tonneau cover fitment because the two generations have different bed lengths and different rail geometries. A cover designed for the 2022+ Frontier will not fit a 2005–2021 model, and vice versa. Always confirm your exact model year before selecting a Worksport SKU. 📏 Frontier Bed Sizes at a Glance Second generation (2005–2021): • King Cab: 5'0" (59.5" usable) short bed • Crew Cab / Long Bed King Cab: 6'0" bed Third generation (2022–present): • King Cab / Crew Cab short bed: 5'0" (60.1") bed • Crew Cab / Long Bed: 6'1" (73.3") bed Tip: If you are not sure which bed size you have, measure the inside bed length from the inside of the bulkhead to the inside of the tailgate, gate closed. 🧰 Does Your Frontier Have the Utility Track System? Many Nissan Frontier trims — especially the PRO-4X, SV, and SL — come equipped from the factory with a Utility Track System (UTS): a set of removable, sliding rails built into the top of the bed walls. This system lets owners attach factory and aftermarket accessories without drilling. Several Worksport SC3 listings for the Frontier specifically note "with or without Utility Track" compatibility. This means those covers are designed to work regardless of whether your UTS rails are present or removed. If you are in doubt, check your truck's build sheet or look inside the bed walls — the UTS rails appear as grooved aluminum extrusions running the length of the bed. 📦 Worksport AL4 — Hard Flip-Up (Frontier) 🎬 Watch AL4 in Action The AL4 is Worksport's Made in USA hard flip-up aluminum cover. It opens on a single hinge at the cab end, swinging all the way forward to give you 100% unrestricted bed access. The low-profile design sits flush with the bed rails for a clean, factory-integrated look. Four locking quick-latches hold the panel secure at every corner. The AL4 for the Frontier is confirmed for both generations. The third-generation (2022+) platform is covered in both the 5'0" and 6'0" bed sizes, with or without the factory Utility Track System. The second-generation (2005–2021) Frontier is covered only in the 6'0" long bed, and only without the Utility Track System installed. Gen 3 (2022–2026): available in both 5'0" and 6'0" beds, with or without the Utility Track System. Gen 2 (2005–2021): available only in the 6'0" long bed, without Utili-Track. No AL4 fitment exists for the gen 2 5'0" short bed. 🛡️ Worksport AL3 — Hard Tri-Fold (Frontier) The AL3 is Worksport's Made in USA hard tri-fold aluminum cover. Three panels fold toward the cab in thirds, giving you access to roughly two-thirds of the bed with the cover fully deployed or the full bed with all three panels folded at the cab. It locks into position at the open or closed latch points with Worksport's Quick Latch system. The AL3 for the Frontier fits the 5'0" short bed across both generations — but only on trucks equipped with the factory silver Utility Track System rails. No AL3 fitment exists for the 6'0" or 6'1" bed in either generation. If your Frontier does not have the factory Utili-Track rails, the SC3 is the correct soft cover alternative. Available only in the 5'0" short bed for both gen 2 (2005–2021) and gen 3 (2022–2026), and only on trucks equipped with the factory silver Utility Track System rails. No AL3 fitment exists for the 6'0" or 6'1" Frontier bed in either generation. 🌟 Worksport SC4 — Soft Flip-Up (Frontier) The SC4 is Worksport's Designed in USA soft flip-up cover. Like the AL4 , it opens as a single panel, hinging at the cab bulkhead for full bed access with one hand. The vinyl tarp is double-PVC coated and UV-protected. The SC4 is not currently offered for the Nissan Frontier in any year or bed size. Frontier owners seeking a soft cover should look at the SC3 . ⭐ Worksport SC3 — Soft Tri-Fold (Frontier) The SC3 is Worksport's Designed in USA soft tri-fold cover. Three fabric-over-aluminum panels fold toward the cab, offering a balance of weather protection, easy access, and a low price point. The SC3 is the most affordably-positioned cover in the Worksport lineup and is the only model with confirmed fitment spanning both Frontier generations. The SC3 is confirmed for both generations of Frontier. For the gen 2 (2005–2021), both the 5'0" and 6'0" beds are covered. For the gen 3 (2022+), only the 5'0" short bed is available in the SC3 — the 6'0" long bed is not offered in the SC3 for the third generation. Gen 2 (2005–2021): available in both 5'0" and 6'0" beds with Utility Track Brackets. Gen 3 (2022–2025): available only in the 5'0" short bed, with or without Utility Track. No SC3 fitment exists for the gen 3 6'0" long bed. 💪 Nissan Titan: The Full-Size Option The Nissan Titan has been sold in its current second-generation form since 2016. Most Worksport covers target the gen 2 Titan (2016–2024), but the SC3 also covers the first-generation Titan (2004–2015) in both bed sizes — a rare find for an older Nissan truck. However, the Titan comes in two cab and bed configurations that matter for cover fitment: • Crew Cab: 5'6" bed — the most common configuration (Worksport selector classification) • King Cab: 6'6" bed — the longer-bed option (Worksport selector classification) The Titan XD is a separate, heavier-duty variant with its own distinct bed sizes. No Worksport fitment was confirmed for the Titan XD via the live vehicle selector; contact Worksport support at 1-888-554-8789 to confirm availability for Titan XD configurations. 📦 Worksport AL4 — Hard Flip-Up (Titan) The AL4 's single-panel flip-up design is well suited to Titan owners who frequently need full unrestricted bed access — loading large equipment, a jobsite tool chest, or oversize gear. The all-aluminum construction and Made in USA heritage appeal to Titan buyers who prioritize durability. The AL4 is confirmed for the gen 2 Titan (2016–2024) in the 5'6" Crew Cab bed, with or without the factory Utility Track System. Available for the gen 2 Titan (2016–2024) in the 5'6" Crew Cab bed, with or without the Utility Track System. No AL4 fitment exists for the 6'6" King Cab bed. 🛡️ Worksport AL3 — Hard Tri-Fold (Titan) The AL3 is a confirmed hard tonneau cover for the Nissan Titan, available for the 2016–2024 model years on the 5'6" Crew Cab bed. The tri-fold design is popular among Titan owners who want hard cover security without sacrificing all cargo access — fold one or two panels back for partial access, or stack all three panels at the cab for the full bed. No AL3 fitment exists for the 6'6" King Cab bed. Available for the gen 2 Titan (2016–2024) in the 5'6" Crew Cab bed only. No AL3 fitment exists for the 6'6" King Cab bed. 🌟 Worksport SC4 — Soft Flip-Up (Titan) The SC4 is Worksport's Designed in USA soft flip-up cover. Like the AL4 , it opens as a single panel, hinging at the cab bulkhead for full bed access. The SC4 is not currently offered for the Nissan Titan in any year or bed size. Titan owners seeking a soft cover should consider the SC3 for the tri-fold option. Confirmed via live selector (worksport.com/products/sc4). The SC3 is the recommended soft cover for all Titan configurations. ⭐ Worksport SC3 — Soft Tri-Fold (Titan) The SC3 is the entry-level soft cover for the Titan, offering the lowest cost of entry into the Worksport lineup. The tri-fold panel design folds toward the cab in thirds and is secured by the same snap-on fabric clamping system used across the SC range. Notably, the SC3 is the only Worksport cover confirmed for the first-generation Titan (2004–2015) — covering both the 5'6" and 6'6" bed in that era. Gen 1 (2004–2015): available in both the 5'6" and 6'6" beds. Gen 2 (2016–2024): available in both the 5'6" and 6'6" beds. Note: the correct bed classification is 5'6" and 6'6" — not 5'7" or 6'7" as listed in some third-party sources. 🔥 Worksport NEXUS — Hard Folding Cover with Single-Side Uplatch The NEXUS is Worksport’s newest hard aluminum cover, launched April 2026. The proprietary Uplatch system auto-secures both bed rail sides from a single point of operation — no walking around the truck. 16-gauge aluminum with DiamondSHIELD finish. Full bed access when panels fold toward the cab. MSRP $1,249–$1,349. Made in the USA. NEXUS fitment for the Nissan Frontier is confirmed for the 3rd generation (2022–2025) only in both the 5’0” and 6’0” beds. The 2nd generation Frontier (2005–2021) is not currently offered for NEXUS . Nissan Titan NEXUS fitment was not confirmed via retailer listings — verify on the Worksport live vehicle selector before publishing. NEXUS is confirmed for the 3rd gen Frontier (2022+) only — the 2005–2021 2nd gen Frontier is not currently offered. Nissan Titan NEXUS fitment was not confirmed via retailer listings; verify on the Worksport live vehicle selector (worksport.com/products/nexus) before publishing. ☀️ Worksport SOLIS — Solar Hard Folding Cover (Frontier & Titan) The SOLIS is Worksport’s integrated solar tonneau cover — a hard folding aluminum cover with embedded solar panels that charge your devices and accessories directly from the sun. SOLIS is available in three tiers based on bed size: Small (~5’0” beds, up to 300W, $1,999), Medium (~5’6”–5’8” beds, up to 380W, $2,249), and Large (6’4”+ beds, up to 600W, $2,499). For the Nissan Frontier: the 5’0” bed fits the Small tier (up to 300W) and the 6’0” bed fits the Medium tier (up to 380W). For the Nissan Titan: the 5’6” Crew Cab bed fits the Medium tier and the 6’6” King Cab bed fits the Large tier. See the SOLIS buying guide GUIDE for full details. 📊 Quick Comparison: All Worksport Covers at a Glance The table below summarizes confirmed fitment for all Worksport covers on the Nissan Frontier and Titan, as verified via the live Worksport vehicle selector. Cover Style Material Nissan Frontier Nissan Titan AL4 Flip-up hard Aluminum 2005–2026 (gen 2: 6' only; gen 3: 5' & 6') 2016–2024 (5'6" only) AL3 Tri-fold hard Aluminum 2005–2026 (5' only — Utili-Track req'd) 2016–2024 (5'6" only) NEXUS Hard fold — Uplatch 16-ga. aluminum 2022–2025 (Gen 3 only) Not confirmed SC4 Flip-up soft Vinyl Not currently offered Not currently offered SC3 Tri-fold soft Vinyl 2005–2025 (gen 2: 5' & 6'; gen 3: 5' only) 2004–2024 (5'6" & 6'6") SOLIS Hard fold + solar Solar aluminum 2005–2026 (Small/Med tier) 2004–2024 (Med/Large tier) 🎯 Which Cover Is Right for Your Frontier? If you own a 2022 or newer Frontier, the AL4 is the premium choice — hard shell, full flip-up access, and the cleanest look in the lineup. The AL3 is the go-to if you prefer tri-fold access and your truck has the factory silver Utili-Track rails (required for the AL3 ). The SC3 covers the 5'0" gen 3 bed and is the right pick if you want a soft cover at a lower price. If you own a 2005–2021 Frontier, the AL4 covers the 6'0" long bed, and the AL3 covers the 5'0" short bed if your truck has the factory silver Utili-Track rails. The SC3 is the confirmed option in both bed sizes. It is a solid cover — weather-resistant, quick to install, and available with utility track bracket hardware that works with your factory UTS rail system. 🧭 Which Cover Is Right for Your Titan? Titan owners with a Crew Cab (5'6" bed) have both the AL4 and AL3 as confirmed hard cover options for 2016–2024. The AL4 gives you full flip-up access; the AL3 gives you tri-fold panel access. The SC3 is the confirmed soft cover for the 5'6" Crew Cab bed across both generations (2004–2024). Titan owners with a King Cab (6'6" bed) have the SC3 as the confirmed soft cover option for 2004–2024. The SC4 is not currently offered for the Titan in any configuration. For hard cover options on the 6'6" bed, contact Worksport directly to confirm availability. 🇺🇸 Made in USA vs. Designed in USA — What It Means for Your Cover Worksport's AL4 and AL3 are Made in USA — designed, engineered, and manufactured domestically. The SC4 and SC3 are Designed in USA, meaning Worksport's engineering team developed the specifications and quality standards in the US, with production handled to those standards globally. Both designations represent genuine Worksport quality — the distinction is primarily relevant for buyers who specifically prioritize domestic manufacturing. ❓ Frequently Asked Questions Will a Frontier tonneau cover fit a Titan? No. The Frontier and Titan use entirely different bed dimensions and rail profiles. Worksport part numbers are specific to each truck — a cover purchased for a Frontier cannot be adapted to fit a Titan, and vice versa. My 2019 Frontier has the Utility Track System. Do I need a special cover? Most Worksport Frontier SC3 listings are explicitly noted as compatible "with or without Utility Track." This means the cover accommodates both configurations. If your specific trim level has the UTS rails, the hardware in the box will include the appropriate utility bracket adapters. Does Worksport make a cover for the Nissan Titan XD? No Titan XD fitment was confirmed via the Worksport live vehicle selector. The Titan XD has distinct bed dimensions from the standard Titan, and no dedicated Worksport SKU was found for it. Contact Worksport customer support at 1-888-554-8789 to confirm if any cover is compatible with your specific Titan XD configuration. Is the AL3 available for the Nissan Frontier's 5'0" short bed? Yes — the AL3 is confirmed for the 5'0" short bed on both gen 2 (2005–2021) and gen 3 (2022–2026) Frontiers. However, the AL3 requires the factory silver Utility Track System rails to be installed. If your Frontier does not have the factory Utili-Track rails, the SC3 is the correct soft cover alternative for the short bed. 🛒 Find the Right Worksport Cover for Your Nissan Use Worksport's interactive vehicle selector at worksport.com ( https://www.worksport.com ) to confirm exact fitment for your year, model, and bed size. Select Year → Make → Model → Bed Size, and the selector will return every cover available for your specific configuration. Questions? Worksport's team is available at 1-888-554-8789, Monday–Friday 9am–9pm ET and Saturday–Sunday 10am–3pm ET. 🎁 Blog Exclusive Offer: Use code BLOG10 at checkout to get $10 off your Worksport order. ← Return to Blog

title: Beyond Meat®, First in the Plant-based Meat Category to Achieve Clean Label Project Certification, Expands Its Certified Portfolio
body_text: With more than 20 products now Clean Label Project Certified, the company continues to expand its leadership in clean, simple ingredients and rigorous third-party standards Newly certified products include Beyond Steak® Filet, Beyond Ground™ Original and Beyond Immerse™ in Peach Mango, Orange Tangerine and Lemon Lime — the first ready-to-drink protein drinks to earn this distinction El Segundo, CALIF. (March 19, 2026) — Beyond Meat, Inc. (NASDAQ: BYND), otherwise known as Beyond The Plant Protein Company™, today announced that more than 20 products across its portfolio have earned Clean Label Project Certification — a designation awarded following rigorous third-party testing for environmental contaminants and harmful substances, including heavy metals and pesticides, and validation in line with strict purity standards. The milestone reinforces the company’s mission to create clean, simple products made with quality ingredients and backed by transparency and accountability. As the first company to earn Clean Label Project Certification for plant-based meat products — including Beyond Burger®, Beyond Beef®, Beyond Steak® and Beyond Chicken® Pieces — the brand sets a new benchmark for transparency and purity. With today’s announcement, the company expands its Clean Label Project Certified portfolio to include Beyond Steak Filet, Beyond Ground Original and Beyond Immerse protein drinks in Peach Mango, Orange Tangerine and Lemon Lime – the first ready-to-drink protein drinks to earn this recognition. “Third-party certifications like Clean Label Project validate the standards we hold ourselves to every day as we deliver the power of plants to the consumer. Our commitment to clean and healthful ingredients defines us, and we are pleased to see this external recognition,” said Ethan Brown, Founder and CEO of Beyond Meat. “Earning Clean Label Project Certification across more than 20 products demonstrates Beyond Meat’s continued focus on transparency and product quality,” said Molly Hamilton, Executive Director of Clean Label Project. “Our program is designed to recognize brands that take proactive steps to evaluate and address contaminants in the products consumers rely on every day. These certifications underscore Beyond Meat’s commitment to accountability and exceeding the status quo.” The Clean Label Project awards certification to products that meet its rigorous standards for purity and safety through comprehensive, independent testing. Products are evaluated for environmental contaminants and harmful substances — including heavy metals, pesticides, plasticizers and other toxins — and are measured against strict health-based benchmarks that often exceed minimum regulatory requirements. Only those products that meet these elevated standards for contaminant safety, ingredient integrity and transparency earn Clean Label Project Certification. For more information about Beyond Meat and its Clean Label Project Certified products, visit www.beyondmeat.com . About Clean Label Project Clean Label Project is a national nonprofit focused on health and transparency in consumer products. Through independent testing for environmental contaminants and public education, Clean Label Project aims to bring truth and transparency to food and consumer product labeling. About Beyond Meat Beyond Meat, Inc. (NASDAQ: BYND), otherwise known as Beyond The Plant Protein Company™, is a plant protein company offering a portfolio of plant-based products made from simple ingredients without GMOs, no added hormones or antibiotics, and 0mg of cholesterol per serving. Founded in 2009, Beyond Meat’s core products are designed to have the same taste and texture as animal-based meat while being better for people and the planet. The company’s brand promise, Eat What You Love®, represents a strong belief that there is a better way to feed our future and that the positive choices we all make, no matter how small, can have a great impact on our personal health and the health of our planet. By shifting from animal-based protein to plant-based protein, we can positively impact four growing global issues: human health, climate change, constraints on natural resources and animal welfare. body_text: Cadeler Takes Delivery of 11th Vessel: Wind Ace July 17, 2026 2:25 am EDT Download as PDF COPENHAGEN, Denmark--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cadeler today announces the successful delivery, within budget and on schedule, of Wind Ace, the company's eleventh wind installation vessel and second of three A-class newbuilds. Cadeler’s A-class vessels are industry leading in flexibility and scope, capable of conversion from the installation of XXL foundations to the installation of wind turbine generators within a short period of time. Wind Ace has been under construction for the past two years at the COSCO Shipping Offshore shipyard in Qidong, China, and has been delivered on schedule, within budget, and with a strong safety record during construction, by reaching more than 3.5 million working hours without any lost time accidents. Following mobilisation, Wind Ace will prepare for deployment on ScottishPower Renewables' East Anglia TWO offshore wind farm in the UK. Cadeler will provide the transportation and installation of both foundations and wind turbines for the project, further building on the company's experience as a full-scope offshore wind installation partner. The vessel was officially named earlier this year by her godmother, Lisa Western of ScottishPower Renewables, recognising the close partnership between the two companies and Wind Ace's future role in the delivery of East Anglia TWO. As the second vessel in Cadeler's A-class series, Wind Ace is purpose-built for the transportation and installation of both XXL monopile foundations and next-generation wind turbine generators. summary: Order entry is the easy part. See why cross-referencing accuracy and AI confidence scoring decide which AI actually grows a distributor's revenue.
body_text: How Distributors Should Evaluate AI: Cross-Referencing and Match Accuracy Are the Hard Part By Jason Sullivan, Founder and CEO, Distro Short answer: When a distributor evaluates AI, the deciding factor is not how fast the tool reads an order. Reading a purchase order or RFQ is the easy part, and nearly every tool will soon do it well. What separates AI that grows revenue from AI you abandon by spring is how accurately it cross-references messy inputs to the right product in your own catalog, and whether it tells your people when it is not sure. Start with the front office, your quoting and sales team, because that is where AI turns into more quotes won and more revenue. Where should a distributor start with AI? Start with the front office. AI can go almost anywhere in a distribution business, from the warehouse to accounts payable, and plenty of it is worth doing. But the front office, your quoting and sales team, is where the money is made and where the retirement wave will hit hardest, whether it has reached you yet or not. AI built for that work gets more quotes out the door and wins more of them. That is what grows revenue, and it is not what most demos are selling you. Why is order entry the easy part of AI for distributors? Reading the document is the easy part. Most AI demos are built around one moment designed to get a reaction: someone drops a messy order or an RFQ into the software, and it pulls every line off the page in seconds, even the notes scribbled in the margin. The room is impressed, but that is the whole point of it, and not much comes after. Pulling text off a page is close to solved and will soon be table stakes for every tool. On its own, it has not won you a single job. What actually matters: cross-referencing to your catalog The value is in what happens after the read. Cross-referencing is the work of matching an incoming line, such as a competitor's part number or a loose description, to the right product in your own catalog, at the right price, with the right substitution. A line on a page is not a quote yet. The part number might be a competitor's, or something you quit stocking two years ago. Sometimes there is no number at all, just "1-1/2 inch bronze circulator, flanged." The right answer is the Taco or the Bell & Gossett you actually carry, at the price this customer gets, with the substitution your best counter person would have reached for without thinking. This is the product knowledge your veterans built up over decades and carry in their heads. It decides whether a quote goes out fast and right or slow and wrong. Get it wrong and you lose the quote, or worse, win it with the wrong part. A distributor told me recently that the quotes that kill his team are not the ones for products he already stocks. Those are easy. It is the ones built around a brand he does not carry, where his people have to cross them over to what he does. Two of his salespeople will cross the same competitor product to two different part numbers, because there is no standard way to do it. That is where the time goes, and where they lose deals. Why does AI confidence scoring matter as much as accuracy? An AI tool has to know how sure it is. A shaky match cannot look as confident as a solid one. The tool has to flag the doubtful ones and say, in effect, "double-check me here." When it does not, the failure is predictable: one of your best people gets a confident answer that is flat wrong, stops trusting the tool, and within a week the whole team is back to the old way. Speed means nothing if no one trusts the results enough to use them. What questions should you ask an AI vendor? When the demo wraps up, keep asking: How do you match a line to the right product when the part number is wrong or missing? How accurate is that matching on my catalog, not a generic one? How do you handle competitor cross-references and substitutions? How does the tool tell my people when it is not sure? A tool that reads an order beautifully but fumbles those questions always looks better in the conference room than on a Tuesday afternoon with a customer on hold. How is this different from order-entry tools like Canals? Most AI sold to distributors is built to read the document. Order-entry and extraction platforms, including tools like Canals and Conexiom, are designed to turn a purchase order or RFQ into structured data quickly. That is useful, but it is the easy part, and it stops short of the work that wins the deal. Reading a line is not the same as knowing which product it maps to in your catalog, at your price, with the right substitution, and how confident that match is. Cross-referencing and confidence scoring are a different and much harder problem, and they are not what an extraction tool is built to do. That gap is exactly where Distro focuses. How Distro approaches cross-referencing and confidence This is the exact problem we built Distro to solve: the cross-referencing and the confidence behind it, not just reading the page. Distro cross-references incoming lines to the right item in a distributor's own catalog more than 90% of the time, and it flags the lines it is not sure about instead of bluffing. That standard holds whether you buy from us or not. Put your money on the hard part, the part that helps your front office sell, and hold any vendor to it. AI really is part of the answer for distributors, as long as you point it at the right place. Reading the order was never the hard part. Turning it into the right product, quoted fast and at a margin you can live with, is the job. Frequently asked questions Is order entry automation the most important AI feature for distributors? No. Reading and extracting lines from a purchase order or RFQ is the easy part and is quickly becoming a commodity. The higher-value work is cross-referencing those lines to the right product in your catalog and scoring how confident the match is. What is cross-referencing in wholesale distribution? Cross-referencing is matching an incoming line, such as a competitor's part number or a vague description, to the correct product you carry, at the correct price, including the right substitution. It is the core of accurate quoting. How is Distro different from order-entry tools like Canals? Order-entry and extraction tools, such as Canals or Conexiom, are built to read a purchase order or RFQ and turn it into data. Distro goes further: it cross-references each line to the right product in your own catalog, applies your pricing and substitutions, and flags matches it is not confident about. Reading the document is the easy part; cross-referencing and confidence scoring are the hard part, and that is what Distro is built for. How accurate should AI cross-referencing be for distributors? Measure accuracy against your own catalog, not a generic one. Distro cross-references to the right item more than 90% of the time and flags low-confidence matches for human review. Why does AI confidence scoring matter? If a tool presents an uncertain match with the same confidence as a certain one, your team will eventually get burned by a wrong answer and stop trusting it. Flagging uncertain matches is what keeps a tool in daily use. Where should a distributor start with AI? Start in the front office, with quoting and sales, because that is where AI most directly grows revenue by producing more accurate quotes and winning more deals.

(NYSE: OKLO) (“Oklo”), an advanced nuclear technology company, today announced that the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has approved the Documented Safety Analysis (DSA) for Oklo Isotopes’ Groves Isotope Test Reactor in Texas under DOE’s Reactor Pilot Program (RPP). With both the PDSA and DSA approved, Groves moves from the documentation phase into DOE’s final pre-startup review. The remaining steps are DOE’s readiness review and startup approval. Following startup approval, the facility will be authorized to receive and load nuclear fuel, conduct startup testing, and proceed toward first criticality, the point at which a reactor achieves a controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction. Oklo is targeting first criticality for Groves in July 2026. “When the Administration issued its Executive Order calling for multiple advanced reactors to go critical outside the national laboratories, it challenged the industry to demonstrate a new way forward,” said Oklo co-founder and CEO Jacob DeWitte. “Groves is that demonstration. It is the first advanced reactor project to receive approval of its Documented Safety Analysis that is on privately owned land, with wholly commercially sourced fuel, equipment, and systems delivered by the private sector. And with full, enduring civil construction, and operations led entirely by a private-sector team under DOE oversight. This is a truly representative facility of future commercial facilities that Oklo intends to build and operate.” “With approval of both the Preliminary and Documented Safety Analyses, Groves now moves into the final phase before startup, including readiness review, fuel loading, and criticality,” DeWitte added. “Less than a year after breaking ground, Groves is advancing toward criticality and demonstrating that advanced nuclear can move from an open field to deployment on a commercial timeline and with a commercially representative facility. DOE demonstrated remarkable capabilities to review and reach this milestone for a facility of this type, and for a facility outside of a national laboratory on this timescale. As the first project of this nature to achieve this milestone under the DOE Reactor Pilot Program, Groves provides a blueprint for how the United States can accelerate advanced reactor deployment while maintaining a rigorous, practical safety process.” Groves supports the development of Oklo’s isotope business and helps establish a stronger domestic supply chain for critical isotopes used in cancer diagnosis and treatment, advanced manufacturing, scientific research, space exploration, and national security applications. Many important isotopes are currently sourced from overseas suppliers or produced in aging facilities, creating supply risks for U.S. hospitals, industry, researchers, and government users. By starting with a pilot facility, Oklo’s isotopes business has developed operating procedures, evaluated reactor system performance, will validate production processes, and build dependable domestic isotope production at commercial scale in the US.
